one_month_reasoning: Revised: Booking has not announced its Q3 2026 date. It gave four weeks' notice for the Oct 28, 2025 and Aug 4, 2026 prints, and none had come by Oct 2, so the print is most likely ~Nov 3, after the window (I put ~15% on it falling inside). Events that are in the window: the FOMC on Oct 27-28 (after the Sep 16 hike to 3.75-4.00%), more AI-agent headlines (Meta Muse/Expedia roll-out), the possibility that the FTC files the complaint against Priceline its staff said it would recommend (10-Q, July 2026), and Dutch parity-litigation news. None of these has a clear sign. I removed the expected-beat tilt and the earnings widening. The result is a near-lognormal with a median of ~$159.6 (buyback support roughly offsets AI-headline risk; the Sep 23 closing low was $155.90) and a sigma of ~10-11% with a modestly fat tail (85% at sigma 10%, 15% at sigma 17%) for headline and FOMC risk.

fair_value.method: Equal blend of 14.5x Oct-2027 NTM EPS of ~$12.75 ($185; FY27 $11.75 is a skeptic haircut of ~5% to the $12.37 consensus) and a 7.5% FCF yield on FY27 FCF less SBC of ~$9.8B over ~715M shares = $13.70/share ($183).

inputs_detail.derivation: FY25 adj EPS $228.06 divided by the 25-for-1 split ratio (split effective Apr 2, 2026 per 10-Q).

Skeptic haircut of ~5% to the $12.37 consensus, down from ~8% in round 1. Consensus implies +18% in FY27 on FY26 $10.45. I assume ~+12%: revenue/EBITDA growth of mid-to-high single digits (Q3 guide +4-6%, Middle East indirect effects per the 10-Q), more marketing spend as AI channels (Muse/Expedia, Google AI Mode) raise acquisition costs, and ~6% net share shrink. Q2 GAAP also had $159M of other income, which I treat as non-recurring.
Mid-single-digit EBITDA growth, the $650M transformation-savings run-rate, and ~5-6% share shrink from the $14.5B authorization and ~$10B FCF.

Today ~13.4x NTM consensus ($159 / $11.89). 14.5x allows a small re-rating as the buyback and EPS delivery continue, but stays well below the 17-18x history (eToro, Feb 2026, which predates Muse and eTraveli). Round 1 used 16x on FY27; I lowered it because that rested on that single pre-Muse source.

methods.name: FCF yield
methods.inputs: FY27E FCF ~$10.4B less SBC ~$0.58B = ~$9.8B / ~715M average shares = $13.70/share at 7.5% yield

inputs_detail.derivation: FCF growing ~7%/yr from $9.1B, in line with the H1 2026 growth rate. Mid-year cash is swollen by deferred merchant bookings ($4.2B working-capital inflow in H1), so I do not annualise H1.
H1 2026 SBC was $281M (10-Q cash-flow statement), annualised. Round 1 used ~$0.65B without a source. I deduct it because SBC is a real cost to owners.

The 10-Q shows 44M shares repurchased in H1 2026 for $7.8B and $14.5B of authorization remaining. FCF of ~$10B less ~$1.3B of dividends funds ~45-50M shares/yr at $165-190, about 6% a year, so ~730M at end-2026 and ~690-700M at end-2027, ~715M on average. The round-1 figure of 765M was the lagging Q2 weighted-average diluted count.

Senior notes $20.3B principal, $2B revolver undrawn, against $17.2B cash. Mid-year cash is inflated by deferred merchant bookings. Ignored in the equity FCF yield because FCF is after interest. Credit is not a risk (A-/A3).

The TTM equity FCF yield is ~8% today ($9.54B / ~$120B). 7.5% allows a slight normalisation. Round 1 used 7%, which I raised because the case for a lower yield also leaned on the pre-Muse eToro multiple history.

bear.story: FY27 EPS growth stalls to ~5% at ~$11.0. That is still above FY26 but well below consensus, because AI assistants (Meta Muse with Expedia, Google AI Mode, hotel-chain agentic direct booking) force higher marketing spend or take-rate concessions, Middle East and airfare effects linger, and US consumer confidence fades (Erste downgrade to Hold). Legal overhang builds: the FTC complaint against Priceline, two Dutch foundation claims (hotels and consumers), German hotel parity suits, and Spain CNMC ($472M accrued). The market pays ~10.5x, an 'AI loser' multiple. Buybacks cushion the per-share hit but do not stop the de-rating.

base.story: EPS compounds ~12%/yr through mid-to-high single-digit growth, cost savings and ~6%/yr share shrink. NTM EPS at Oct 2027 is ~$12.6. The AI overhang stays but does not deepen, and the multiple holds near 13.9x NTM, roughly today's level.

bull.story: Consensus-plus delivery (NTM EPS ~$13.4). Booking shows it is the supply layer AI agents route through (agent partnerships, stable marketing efficiency), travel normalises after the Middle East conflict, and litigation is contained. The multiple recovers to ~17x, back toward the 52-week high.

thesis_break_reason: Below ~$118 the stock would trade at ~10x my haircut FY27 EPS ($11.75) and ~9.5x consensus, with a ~12% FCF yield, ~21% below the $150.14 52-week low. With ~6%/yr of buyback shrink supporting the stock, that level would most likely mean estimates are falling: room nights flat or negative, take-rate or marketing-cost damage from AI channels, a multi-billion parity-damages ruling or FTC settlement, or a travel recession. A de-rating alone would be unlikely to get there.

reasoning: Round 2 (skeptic). Supervisor findings accepted: (1) Shares outstanding were 751.4M on Jul 27, 2026 and are falling ~6%/yr (44M retired in H1, $14.5B left), not 765M. I checked this in the 10-Q equity statement, and it lifts my FCF leg by roughly $15 at constant inputs. (2) Consensus FY26/FY27 is $10.45/$12.37. My FY27 is now an explicit ~5% haircut ($11.75), down from the 8% implied by $11.40, which the supervisor rightly called unlabelled. I keep a haircut because consensus needs +18% EPS growth in FY27 while Q3 EBITDA is guided at +4-6%. (3) The Q3 print is likely ~Nov 3, outside the 1-month window, so I narrowed the 1m ladder and removed the beat tilt. (4) The recent closing low was Sep 23 ($155.90), not Sep 17. (5) The supervisor asked whether my bear EPS of $10.5 was consistent with low-to-mid-teens guidance. It was not, since it implied earnings flat to down from FY26. The bear EPS is now $11.0 (+5%), and the bear price moves from $120 to $116 at 10.5x. Where I disagree: I do not adopt 16x on FY27 or a 7% yield, because both leaned on the single pre-Muse eToro source the supervisor flagged. I use 14.5x NTM and a 7.5% yield, with both legs now on corrected per-share figures. New skeptic evidence from the 10-Q (primary source, replacing blog recaps): the FTC staff intend to recommend a complaint against Priceline over fees, disclosures and billing. Beyond the hotel claim there is a Dutch consumer-foundation claim alleging misleading practices by Booking.com and Agoda. German hotels have ongoing parity suits, and class actions in Spain, France and the UK are possible. None of these is accrued except the CNMC ($472M). There is also $313M of unrecognised tax benefits and reliance on the Dutch Innovation Box (9% vs 25.8%). Erste moved to Hold citing US consumer confidence. Credit is still clean: $20.3B of senior notes and the $2B revolver undrawn. Net: fair value rises from $180 to $184, and the scenario mean from $171 to ~$175 (bear $116/23%, base $175/52%, bull $228/25%). The ladder is a lognormal mixture (spreads 17-22%) with tails fattened toward 38% realized vol. P(>=159) is 0.625 and the median is ~$175. Research was limited to the 10-Q (primary) and one search.
